novel_features.name: SoC/range trends
novel_features.description: See your battery state-of-charge and derived range as a time series you can chart.
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining retained telematic snapshots over time in local SQLite — no single API call or existing tool gives you history.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this when an agent needs SoC/range history or trend direction instead of a single live snapshot.

novel_features.name: Charging cost & efficiency
novel_features.description: Reconcile your charging sessions against your electricity tariff and see DC charge efficiency.
novel_features.rationale: Joins charging sessions (kWh, duration) with a user tariff locally and computes per-session DC efficiency — impossible without a local store.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this when an agent must turn raw charging sessions into money spent and charging efficiency.

novel_features.name: Quota tracker
novel_features.description: See how many of your ~50 daily API calls you have spent and when the budget resets (midnight UTC).
novel_features.rationale: Computed locally from sync metadata; BMW enforces a hard daily cap that silently fails commands — only a local counter can warn before it hits.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this before any sync or polling loop so an agent does not burn the daily quota and start failing.

novel_features.name: Fleet status
novel_features.description: One table of current SoC, range, charging state and last location across every vehicle on your account.
novel_features.rationale: Cross-joins vehicles with the latest telematic snapshot per VIN locally — the API only returns one VIN at a time and no tool gives a multi-car view.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this when an agent needs a single multi-vehicle overview instead of calling each VIN separately.

novel_features.name: Descriptor search
novel_features.description: Search the VSS telematic descriptor catalogue (e.g. batteryManagement, charging, navigation) to build containers.
novel_features.rationale: FTS over a seeded local copy of BMW's telematic data catalogue — the spec lists descriptors as opaque strings with no searchable index.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this when an agent needs to discover the exact VSS descriptor paths to put in a container.

novel_features.name: Battery health
novel_features.description: Track battery capacity degradation by comparing observed max energy against the nameplate capacity.
novel_features.rationale: Joins the nameplate hvsMaxEnergyAbsolute from basicData with the max observed energy across history — needs retained snapshots.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this when an agent must report long-term battery degradation rather than current state of charge.

novel_features.name: Snapshot diff
novel_features.description: Show exactly what changed between two telematic snapshots (windows, charging, locks, location).
novel_features.rationale: Field-by-field diff over retained snapshot history — only possible because the CLI stores every snapshot locally.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this when an agent needs discrete state changes (did charging start? did a window open?) not a numeric level.

novel_features.name: Trip reconstruction
novel_features.description: Reconstruct trips (start, end, elapsed, distance) from your vehicle's location breadcrumbs.
novel_features.rationale: Segments the navigation.currentLocation time-series into trips locally — the API streams points, never trips.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this when an agent needs driven trips and distances rather than raw GPS points.

narrative.headline: Your BMW's telemetry, on the command line — live snapshots, charging history, and a local SQLite store for trends and fleet insight no other tool offers.
narrative.value_prop: BMW CarData is the official, free-for-personal-use API for your own vehicle data. This CLI handles the OAuth device-code onboarding, fetches live telematic snapshots, charging history and tyre diagnosis, then keeps it all in SQLite so you can chart SoC trends (soc-trends), reconcile charging cost against your tariff (charging-cost), and see every vehicle at once (fleet status).
narrative.auth_narrative: BMW CarData uses an OAuth2 Device Code Flow with PKCE. First, generate a client_id in the BMW CarData portal (My BMW > BMW CarData > Create CarData Client; tick 'Request access to CarData API', and 'CarData Stream' if you want streaming) and save it — the portal hides it on reload. Then run `bmw-cardata-pp-cli auth login`, open the printed verification URL, log in to BMW, and approve. The CLI stores the access and refresh tokens locally and refreshes them automatically. You can also export BMW_CARDATA_CLIENT_ID and run auth login non-interactively. Requires an EU vehicle with an active SIM, a ConnectedDrive contract, and the vehicle mapped to your account as the primary user.

quickstart.comment: Health check; works before any auth is configured.
One-time device-code onboarding (generate a client_id in the BMW portal first).
List the VINs mapped to your account.
Fetch live telematic data for a container, narrowing the nested VSS payload (also writes through to local store).
Transcendence: SoC/range trend from your local SQLite store.

troubleshoots.symptom: Commands start returning 429 / quota_exceeded late in the day
troubleshoots.fix: Run `bmw-cardata-pp-cli quota`; BMW caps ~50 calls/day per client resetting at midnight UTC — rely on the local store and `sync` instead of repeated live calls.
Open the printed verification_uri_complete in a browser, log in to BMW, and approve the device; polling continues until you do or the code expires.

troubleshoots.symptom: auth fails with invalid_client after regenerating a client
troubleshoots.fix: The portal hides the client_id on reload — re-create the CarData client, save the new id, and set BMW_CARDATA_CLIENT_ID before `auth login`.

troubleshoots.symptom: stream connects but no data arrives
troubleshoots.fix: Re-create the CarData client with 'CarData Stream' enabled and subscribe to the events you want; streaming permissions can only be set at client creation.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when you want programmatic, scriptable, or agent-driven access to your own BMW/MINI/Rolls-Royce/Supra vehicle telemetry over the official CarData API — fetching live snapshots, syncing charging history, or analysing trends across time and vehicles. It is ideal for Home Assistant users, data-sovereignty tinkerers, and anyone who wants their car's data in SQLite rather than trapped in an app.
anti_triggers: Do not use for remote vehicle commands (lock/unlock, honk, climate) — CarData is read-only telemetry; use the My BMW app or ConnectedDrive remote services.
Do not use outside supported EU markets or without an active ConnectedDrive contract + SIM; the API will return 403.
Do not use as a real-time high-frequency feed without checking `quota` first; the ~50 calls/day cap resets at midnight UTC.
Do not use the B2B / partner CarData API path from this CLI; this targets the free personal customer API only.

recipes.title: Narrow a deeply nested telematic payload for an agent
recipes.explanation: telematicData returns every descriptor as a nested {value,unit,timestamp} map; --select trims it to just the battery and charging keys so an agent does not parse tens of KB.

recipes.title: Reconcile last month's charging against your tariff
recipes.explanation: Joins synced charging sessions with a per-kWh price locally to report money spent and DC efficiency.

recipes.title: One-glance multi-car status
recipes.explanation: Cross-joins every mapped VIN with its latest telematic snapshot for SoC, range, charging state and location.

recipes.title: Watch today's API budget before syncing
recipes.explanation: Reads the local call counter against the ~50/day cap and reports the midnight-UTC reset time.

recipes.title: Build a container from searched descriptors
recipes.command: bmw-cardata-pp-cli customers create-container --technical-descriptors $(bmw-cardata-pp-cli descriptors search batteryManagement --json | jq -r ".[].path") --dry-run
recipes.explanation: Search the VSS catalogue, then create a container of matching descriptors with a dry-run preview.
